# Twitter(X).com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/twitter-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/twitter-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects public X.com (formerly Twitter) posts and user data, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape X.com (Twitter) using Python (2025 Update)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-twitter)
- **Code:** [`twitter.py`](twitter.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Profile pages](results/profile.json) · [Tweet pages](results/tweet.json)

## What it scrapes

- X.com post data
- X.com user profile data

## Functions

- `scrape_tweet(url)` → `Dict`: scrape a tweet page
- `scrape_profile(url)` → `Dict`: scrape a profile page

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import twitter


async def main():
    tweet = await twitter.scrape_tweet("https://x.com/robinhanson/status/1872047986873885082")
    profile = await twitter.scrape_profile("https://x.com/robinhanson/")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/profile.json`](results/profile.json): `id`, `rest_id`, `name`, `screen_name`, `verified`, `description`, `location`, `joined`, `url`, `profile_image_url`, `profile_banner_url`, `followers_count`, `friends_count`, `statuses_count`, `fast_followers_count`, `entities`
- [`results/tweet.json`](results/tweet.json): `id`, `conversation_id`, `url`, `text`, `created_at`, `language`, `attached_urls`, `attached_media`, `tagged_users`, `tagged_hashtags`, `reply_count`, `retweet_count`, `favorite_count`, `bookmark_count`, `views`, `user`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`twitter.py`](twitter.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `auto_scroll` = `True`: scroll the page to load lazy content
- `rendering_wait` = `2000`: wait after the page rendered, in milliseconds
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Notes

What is NOT possible to scrape without login through X.com website:

- Post replies
- Post search

Note: This scraper is only scraping public Twitter data that doesn't require a login to access.

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/twitter-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_tweet_scraping`, `test_user_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
